tone.target: thick vintage fuzz-crunch with bluesy mid bite
tone.profile: thick vintage fuzz-crunch with bluesy mid bite
tone.summary: Gate -> Boost (OD 9) -> Fuzz -> UK 45 Amp -> UK Vintage 4x12 Cab -> EQ -> Chorus -> Plate Reverb

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and stray noise inherent in vintage fuzz tones.
Provide initial grit and boost the signal into the fuzz stage.
blocks.gap: Using Boost for general tone shaping before the main distortion, as a dedicated pre-amp isn't strictly necessary here.

alternatives.reason: Could also work to add initial grit.

blocks.purpose: Achieve the required thick vintage fuzz-crunch and saturation.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative for a different type of grit.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Plexi/early British tone and provide mid-forward punch.

alternatives.reason: Similar vintage British sound, but UK 45 is more associated with the Plexi era.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet sound and vintage texture.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative for a slightly different UK flavor.

blocks.purpose: Sculpt the tone to emphasize bluesy mid-bite and control low end bloat.
Add subtle vintage movement and width without distracting from the fuzz core.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used sparingly to add depth, as requested by 'vintage texture', but it must be kept minimal.

alternatives.reason: Could provide movement, but Chorus better suits the vintage fullness.

blocks.purpose: Add minimal ambient space and vintage room feel without excessive wash.
blocks.gap: The reverb must be kept very low to maintain the aggressive, dry fuzz character.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative for a more natural room ambience.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better vintage British cabinet realism.

proposals.reason: Enhance the authentic Plexi/early Vox British tone and mono feel.
